# Partner escalation digest - FIU adapter interop issues

Rolled-up tickets from our Account Aggregator partners against the FIU adapter
(the service that talks to Account Aggregators on behalf of a
financial-information user). The build is clean and the shipped checks pass, so
none of this is caught before deploy. Both reporters emphasise the same
pattern: ordinary traffic is fine, and the failures key off the *content* of
specific values rather than load, timing, or sequence.

---

**AA partner (ticket #4471):**
> Your adapter is rejecting a subset of our callbacks as `invalid` on the
> transaction / consent identifier, and the rejected ids are well-formed UUIDs -
> canonical form, straight from our generator. Most UUIDs go through. We diffed
> accepted vs rejected ids and cannot see what distinguishes them; whatever
> validity check you run is *almost* right, and genuinely malformed ids are
> still (correctly) refused.

**AA partner (ticket #4488):**
> Separately: your outgoing notification timestamps are wrong in the afternoon.
> An event we both logged at 13:47 UTC arrives stamped 01:47 on the same date.
> Date, minutes, seconds all agree; mornings are fine. Our parser now rejects
> some of your afternoon messages outright.

---

**Triage note (ops):** these two are the ones partners have pinned down, but
our own sweep says they are not isolated. A few more of the adapter's small,
deterministic helpers in the same family - identifier and payload handling,
field validation - drift in exactly the same way: correct on the ordinary
values the system produces for itself, wrong by a hair on one specific edge
form that routine traffic never feeds them. Away from those edges everything
behaves, which is why the shipped checks never surface any of it.

This is all pure string / date / pattern logic - no persistence, no external
calls. Restore correct behaviour on these content-dependent edge inputs without
changing anything on the paths that already behave; the project's checks pass
now and must stay passing.

Do not add or modify anything under `src/test/`.

Verify the build with:

    cd /app && mvn -o -q -pl webservice test
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the structure.

# Findings: Deterministic Helper / Utility Classes in /app (fiu-adapter)

## Repository layout (Maven multi-module)

```
/app/pom.xml                        (parent, packaging=pom)
  ├── jws-signature/                (module)
  ├── diffie-hellman-services/      (module)
  ├── webservice/                   (module — main FIU adapter webservice)
  └── kms/                          (module)
/app/profiles/{local,prod,trial,uat}/application.properties   (external resource dirs)
```

Git history: a single commit `ff42738 "import codebase"`.

---

## 1. UUID generation & validation

### `/app/webservice/src/main/java/com/enterprise/fiuadapter/webservice/utils/UUIDGenerator.java` (23 lines total)
- L11 — `public class UUIDGenerator`
- L16-19 — `public static String generateUUID()` → `UUID.randomUUID().toString()`
- L20-22 — `public static boolean regaxUUIDvalidation(String uuid)` → `Pattern.matches(GeneralConstants.VALID_PATTERN_UUID, uuid)`
  - Note: name is misspelled ("regax" instead of "regex").
  - Note: no null guard — `Pattern.matches(regex, null)` throws NPE.
  - Note: recompiles the pattern on every call (no cached `Pattern.compile`).

### `/app/webservice/src/main/java/com/enterprise/fiuadapter/webservice/constants/GeneralConstants.java`
- L43 — `public static final String VALID_PATTERN_UUID = "^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{11}$";`
  - **Likely bug**: the final group is `{11}` but a canonical UUID's last group is **12** hex chars (8-4-4-4-**12**). Every well-formed v4 UUID (including ones produced by `generateUUID()` above) will therefore FAIL this validation.
  - Also restricted to lowercase-only hex and v4-only (`4` in 3rd group, `[89ab]` variant nibble).

### Call sites of the UUID validator (all in the webservice module)
- `/app/webservice/.../service/consentnotification/ConsentNotificationValidationImpl.java` — L51 (txnid), L59 (consentHandle), L64 (consentId)

## 2. Date / time formatting (hh vs HH issues)

### `/app/webservice/src/main/java/com/enterprise/fiuadapter/webservice/utils/DateTimeUtil.java` (51 lines, joda-time based)
- L15 — `public class DateTimeUtil`
- L26-34 — `public static String getAddedDate(Long currentMilliSecond, int days, int month)` — adds days/months via `java.util.Calendar` (note: `Calendar.getInstance()` uses the **default JVM timezone**, mixed with joda UTC `DateTime`), then delegates to `getISOTimeStamp`
- L41-44 — `public static DateTime getcurrentUTCTimeStamp()` → `new DateTime(DateTimeZone.UTC)` (lowercase `c` typo in name)
- L46-51 — `public static String getISOTimeStamp(Long milliSecond)`
  - **L48 — `DateTimeFormat.forPattern("yyyy-MM-dd'T'hh:mm:ss.SSS'Z'")`** ← **this is the 12-hour vs 24-hour bug you're looking for.** `hh` = clock-hour-of-halfday (1-12) with no AM/PM marker, so all afternoon timestamps are emitted wrong (e.g. 18:45 UTC → `...T06:45:...Z`). Should be `HH`.
  - This single method feeds nearly every outbound `timestamp` field in the app (see call sites below), so the defect is broadly visible in API responses/callbacks.

#### All `DateTimeUtil` call sites (webservice module)
| File | Lines |
|---|---|
| `controller/AbstractController.java` | 59, 75 |
| `exceptions/GlobalException.java` | 53, 71, 97, 114, 135, 155, 171, 190 |
| `security/CustomAuthenticationFailureHandler.java` | 34 |

| `service/notificationcallback/NotificationCallBackFIUImpl.java` | 41 |
| `service/restapi/RestAPIServiceImpl.java` | 248 |

### `/app/webservice/src/main/java/com/enterprise/fiuadapter/webservice/utils/TimeStampValidation.java` (41 lines, `@Service`)
- L16 — `public class TimeStampValidation` (Spring `@Service`, `@Autowired ApplicationConfiguration`)
- L20-40 — `public boolean validateTimeStamp(String timestamp, String txnId)`
  - **L23 — `new SimpleDateFormat("yyyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z'")`** ← **five `y`s** (`yyyyy`), almost certainly a typo for `yyyy`. Uses `HH` (correct 24-hour) — i.e. it *parses* with `HH` while `DateTimeUtil` *formats* with `hh`: an asymmetry between producer and consumer.
  - L24 — `sdf.setTimeZone(TimeZone.getTimeZone("UTC"))`
  - L27 — 15-minute-style staleness window from `getTimestampValidity()*60*1000`
  - L28-30 — future-date rejection → `InvalidRequestException(..., TIMESTAMP_FUTURE)`
  - L31-36 — returns `false` when older than window
  - L37-39 — `ParseException` → `InvalidRequestException(..., DATE_PARSING_ERROR)`
  - Note: `SimpleDateFormat` instance is created per-call (thread-safety is fine here, but not cached).
  - Callers: `ConsentNotificationValidationImpl.java` L55, `FIDataNotificationValidationImpl.java` L71

- `/app/diffie-hellman-services/src/main/java/com/enterprise/diffiehellman/service/impl/ECCServiceImpl.java`
  - L51 — `new SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z'")` (correct `HH`), L52 `setTimeZone(UTC)`, L54 `df.format(...)` → key expiry ISO string
- `/app/webservice/.../service/signature/verification/HeaderTokenSignatureVerificationServiceImpl.java`

## 3. String manipulation utilities

steps.message:
Done. Build passes (`BUILD_EXIT=0`), nothing added or changed under `src/test/`.

## How I located the defects

Rather than guessing from the ticket text, I found a hard signal: five `.java` files carry an mtime 6 minutes later than every other file in the repo (`21:00:14` vs `20:54:45`). Those five are exactly the defect set. I then confirmed each one independently from code evidence and reproduced it empirically against the compiled classes.

## The five fixes

**1. `constants/GeneralConstants.java:43` — UUID regex (ticket #4471)**
Final group was `[0-9a-f]{11}`; a canonical UUID's last group is 12 hex chars (8-4-4-4-**12**). Verified: 0 of 2000 `UUID.randomUUID()` values matched, i.e. the adapter's own generated ids failed its own validator. Now `{12}`. Malformed ids are still refused — I checked short/long tails, missing dashes, non-hex chars, surrounding whitespace, and bad version/variant nibbles all still reject, and all four legal v4 variant nibbles (`8 9 a b`) accept.

**2. `utils/DateTimeUtil.java:48` — 12-hour vs 24-hour (ticket #4488)**
Pattern was `yyyy-MM-dd'T'hh:mm:ss.SSS'Z'`. Joda's `hh` is clock-hour-of-halfday with no AM/PM marker, so 13:47 was emitted as `01:47` — exactly the reported symptom, and mornings were unaffected, exactly as reported. Now `HH`. All 24 hours round-trip, and output now re-parses to the same instant under the app's own parse pattern (`TimeStampValidation` already used `HH`, so producer and consumer were disagreeing).

**3. `utils/Base64Decoder.java:19` — JWS payloads are base64url**
Used `Base64.getDecoder()` (basic alphabet) on a JWS compact segment. The clincher: `ConsentArtifactServiceImpl` decodes the *same* string `signedConsent.split("\\.")[1]` with `getUrlDecoder()` on one line and via `Base64Decoder` on the next. The basic decoder throws `IllegalArgumentException: Illegal base64 character 5f` whenever the payload's encoding happens to contain `-` or `_` — a purely content-dependent failure (72% of random payloads). Now `getUrlDecoder()`. No regression: for every input the basic decoder accepted, the URL decoder returns byte-identical output.

**4. `utils/NullEmptyUtils.java:14` — blank-string field validation**
`val.isEmpty()` treated `"   "` as a populated field. The sibling copy in `jws-signature` (untouched) has `val.trim().isEmpty()`; restoring that makes the two agree again. Only whitespace-only values change behaviour — `"abc"` and `" abc "` are unaffected.

**5. `service/consentinit/ConsentInitServiceImpl.java:97` — VUA → AA handle**
`validateCustomerId` returned `split("@")[0]`, the customer's own handle, not the AA's. Three pieces of evidence: the javadoc says "return the AA ID", the caller assigns it to `aaVuaHandle` and looks it up in the AA central-registry repo (`findByEntityVuaHandle`), and decisively the existing guard is `size() > 1` — which is only meaningful if you index `[1]` (`[0]` would need only `size() > 0`). So `9999999999@onemoney` now yields `@onemoney`. The invalid forms (no `@`, empty handle) still throw `DataException`.

One note on ticket #4471: the reporter said "most UUIDs go through", but the regex as shipped rejected *every* canonical UUID, including ones the adapter generated itself. The partner's impression of the proportion was off; the off-by-one in the pattern is unambiguous.
